newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr edges ahead as RBA stays silent.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr edges ahead as RBA stays silent.

text.p: The Australian dollar edged ahead in thin trade after the Reserve Bank stayed silent at its morning operation, the usual time for a policy announcement.

The market has been discounting a rate cut for weeks and speculation reached fever pitch this week following favourable wage and inflation data. Bill futures have fully priced in a 0.5 point easing in the cash rate to 5.0 percent and that will not change as the market simply expects the bank is waiting for its monthly board meeting on August 5 and will move the day after.
By 9.34 am (2335 GMT) the dollar had crept to US$0.7382/87 from an early US$0.7361/66 and US$0.7348/53 late here Thursday.
The 90-day bank bill future for September inched back two basis points to 94.95 but that still implied a rate of 5.05 percent, showing how confident the market was the RBA would eventually ease.
That in turn was expected to limit any dollar rally and probably keep it beneath the important US$0.7440/75 resistance band until the board meeting.

It was broadly firmer on the crosses amid short covering and heavy fund flows out of the mark and Swiss franc and into the dollar bloc in general. In trade weighted terms it rose to 57.3 from a previous 57.1 close. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
